seo.search_intent: Understand what buckwheat is, its nutrient profile, and whether it is gluten-free.

excerpt: Despite its name, buckwheat is not related to wheat and is naturally gluten-free. Cooked groats provide roughly 92 calories, 3.4 g protein, and 2.7 g fiber per 100 g, plus magnesium, manganese, and plant compounds such as rutin.
content_html:
The name is misleading: buckwheat is not wheat and is not even a botanical cereal grain. It is the seed of Fagopyrum esculentum and is classified as a pseudocereal.

What cooked buckwheat provides

Per 100 g cooked, buckwheat groats are roughly 92 calories, 3.4 g protein, about 20 g carbohydrate, and 2.7 g fiber.

Minerals and plant compounds

Buckwheat contributes magnesium, manganese, and copper and contains flavonoids such as rutin.

Naturally gluten-free

The Celiac Disease Foundation lists buckwheat among naturally gluten-free foods. Cross-contact remains possible in flour and processed products.

How it is used

Toasted groats are called kasha. Buckwheat flour is used in pancakes and soba noodles, but many soba products mix buckwheat with regular wheat flour, so they are not automatically gluten-free.

The “wheat” in the name is culinary history, not a clue about gluten.

faq.question: Does buckwheat contain gluten?
faq.answer: Not naturally. For celiac disease, choose products protected from gluten cross-contact.

faq.question: How much protein is in cooked buckwheat?
Are soba noodles gluten-free?
faq.answer: Not always. Many include wheat flour in addition to buckwheat.
